2.text: Violence on Women. — I mentioned before that Chukchee males are

3.text: often inclined to violence and rape. Thus, in the tale about Scabby-Shaman,

4.text: the young Rɪˊntew, when he has become a “mocking shaman,”¹ begins to act

5.text: quite shamelessly. He runs from tent to tent, from one sleeping-room to

6.text: another. Wheresoever there is a woman, he violates her. Where a man is

7.text: lying quietly, he catches him by the penis, shakes him, and lifts him. When

8.text: he comes to a sleeping-room and finds an old man and old woman sleeping

9.text: there quietly, he enters and catches the man by the penis, tears away his

10.text: breeches, then shoves him here and there, and at last throws him down.

11.text: After that he tears away all clothing from the old woman, takes off every-

12.text: thing, and copulates with her. Throughout the night he runs about from one

13.text: tent to another, acting in this manner. In his great speed he casts away his

14.text: breeches and boots. Thus he runs about naked and violates women.²

15.text: In another tale about Lucky-Suitor, a young man wants to marry a proud

16.text: girl. When she refuses him, he visits her among her herd, catches her, takes

17.text: off all her clothes, then tramples her down into the snow and scratches her

18.text: whole face with the point of his knife. The next year he is severely punished

19.text: for this act by an accepted suitor of the girl.

20.text: I have already mentioned, that, since the young men marry early, sexual

21.text: relations sometimes begin before full maturity is reached. Not infrequently

22.text: very young girls bear children; and, the language contains a special term for

23.text: them, as êčvaˊk-äᵋʟaˊ (“the fawn mother”), which is the same term as that

24.text: applied to a fawn bearing young.³ Some female fawns bear young the first

25.text: spring after their birth, being hardly a year old.

26.text: I mentioned also, that, on the whole, the Chukchee have a notion that

27.text: early marriages are injurious to the health of the woman, and tend to diminish

28.text: the number of births.⁴ Therefore it is held to be equally blameworthy to have

29.text: intercourse with a girl that is not perfectly mature, or, according to a Chukchee

30.text: statement, with one “not having full breasts and the menses.”

31.text: D. J. Melikoff, in his report, states, quoting from Eiˊheli, “the so-called

32.text: general chief of the Chukchee,” whose name has already been mentioned, and

33.text: also from his brother-in-law, Omrêlqoˊt, that with the Chukchee, violence on

34.text: a young girl not perfectly mature is considered to be a serious crime, and

35.text: therefore is severely punished by the Council of the Elders. I mentioned in

36.text: the list of authorities quoted that this report was in manuscript. W. I. Jochelson,⁵
